messages:
Rina K.: kicking off a short thread to align on the benchmark narrative + assets for next week's launch. outcome = 1) 2 hero visuals, 2) 90s launch post, 3) 1-page playbook for sales. who can pair on charts + copy? :sparkles:
Tom S.: I can do the hero visuals. thinking a dual-axis line for cost per request (log) and median latency (ms) across seq lengths. also a small table showing 'typical config' for each point.
Asha W.: i'll own the 90s post and the sales playbook. want callouts for: predictable latency, cost leverage via batching & quantization, and routing policies. keep it technical-messaging first.
Vikram G.: Dataset ready. benchbot exported experiments for: redwood-small, redwood-std, openfam-llama across seq buckets: 32, 128, 512, 2048. metrics: p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_usd, throughput_rps. uploading now.
BenchBot: export link: https://internal.redwood/bench/exports/1725033333/benchset_v3.csv :file_cabinet: 
Rina K.: Good. Tom, Asha: let's avoid "cost savings" without context. prefer "cost-per-inference reduction" and show config footnote: quantized q4, batch 8, A100.
Tom S.: agreed. Visual 1: scatter/sized-bubble: x=p50 latency, y=cost-per-inference, size=throughput, color=model-family, facets=seq_bucket. Visual 2: stacked bar of throughput-per-dollar by batching strategy (no-batch, batch-4, batch-8) per seq bucket.
Asha W.: headline options (need short A/B):
- A: "Serve predictable latency. Spend less on the tail."
- B: "Right-sized inference for real apps: latency you trust, dollars you control."
Which is more product-y?
Rina K.: I prefer B but tighten: "Right-sized inference: latency you trust, dollars you control."
Vikram G.: numbers preview: for doc summarize (2048): q4 + batch8 -> 2.9x tokens_per_usd vs float32 no-batch. for chat short (32): p50 difference <10ms across configs. p95 increases with batching; i'll include p95 appendix.
Asha W.: good, include an engineer-facing footnote: "Bench run: A100, Ubuntu20, TensorRT/opt kernels, model weights quantized to q4x4."
Tom S.: captions: scatter -> "Lower & left = ideal (low latency, low cost)." bubble label for "balanced routing" point. bar chart caption -> "Batching increases throughput-per-dollar, but watch tail latency."
Rina K.: CTA ideas for launch post: 1) "Try the latency-cost playground" -> self-serve demo with sample workloads, 2) "Request a dedicated trial" -> sales path. Also offer webinar sign-up for deeper dive.
Asha W.: i'll draft the post with the two CTAs + a short bulleted list: what we measured, why it matters, how to run your own test. keep it <4 bullets.
Vikram G.: can we add a quick reproducibility note: github link to bench harness + seed configs? happy to anonymize internal hostnames.
Rina K.: yes. include repo: https://github.com/redwood/bench-harness (public). add an Appendix with exact commands: e.g.,
```
python run_benchmark.py --model redwood-std --seq 2048 --quant q4 --batch 8 --hw a100
```
Tom S.: timeline: I'll post initial PNG + SVG by today 5pm to /design/bench-assets and upload thumbnails to notion. Asha: draft copy by tomorrow 10am. Vikram: final verified numbers + appendix by EOD tomorrow.
BenchBot: job queued: compute p95 tails for batch-8 across models. ETA 3h.
Asha W.: one more ask: sales playbook must include two routing presets to recommend: "balanced" (p50 focus) and "tail-guarded" (p95 focus with smaller batches). include suggested SLAs per preset.
Vikram G.: will simulate both presets and produce comparative table: p50, p95, cost-per-1k-tokens.
Rina K.: perfect. we'll iterate in this thread. plan dry-run review on Friday 9:30am. thanks all :raised_hands:
